levels.nameEn: Nice to meet you: who am I?
levels.challengeEs: Preséntate otra vez: tu nombre, de dónde eres, cómo estás hoy y si tienes hambre o sed.
levels.challengeEn: Introduce yourself again: your name, where you are from, how you are today, and whether you are hungry or thirsty.
levels.successEn: Use ser for name and origin (Soy de...), estar for how you feel (Estoy...), and tener for hunger or thirst (Tengo sed).
levels.sampleAnswerEs: Me llamo Alex. Soy de Gainesville. Hoy estoy muy bien, pero tengo mucha sed.
levels.sampleAnswerEn: My name is Alex. I am from Gainesville. Today I am very well, but I am very thirsty.

levels.challengeEs: Ahora tu amiga y tú estudian química. Contesta: ¿de dónde son, qué estudian y cuál es su clase más difícil?
levels.challengeEn: Now you and your friend both study chemistry. Answer: where are you from, what do you study, and which is your hardest class?
levels.successEn: Use plural forms (somos, estamos, estudiamos), agree adjectives, and use cuál to pick from options.
levels.sampleAnswerEs: Somos de Florida. Estudiamos química. Nuestra clase más difícil es física.
levels.sampleAnswerEn: We are from Florida. We study chemistry. Our hardest class is physics.

levels.challengeEs: Lupita te invita a una clase de salsa el viernes a las siete. No puedes ir. Rechaza con cortesía y explica por qué.
levels.challengeEn: Lupita invites you to a salsa class on Friday at seven. You can't go. Decline politely and explain why.
levels.successEn: Use a refusal phrase (¡Qué lástima!), tener que + infinitive for the reason, and ir a + infinitive for another plan.
levels.sampleAnswerEs: ¡Ay, qué lástima! El viernes tengo que trabajar a las siete. Pero voy a ir a la próxima clase.
levels.sampleAnswerEn: Oh, what a shame! On Friday I have to work at seven. But I'm going to go to the next class.

levels.challengeEs: Pregunta si hay una mesa cerca de la ventana, di dónde estudias y qué no te gusta tomar.
levels.challengeEn: Ask if there's a table near the window, say where you study, and say what you don't like to drink.
levels.successEn: Use hay for what exists, estar for where something is, an -ar verb in the yo form, and (no) me gusta/n.
levels.sampleAnswerEs: ¿Hay una mesa cerca de la ventana? Estudio en la biblioteca. No me gusta el café con azúcar.
levels.sampleAnswerEn: Is there a table near the window? I study at the library. I don't like coffee with sugar.

levels.challengeEs: Describe a un amigo que admiras: cómo es, qué hace y por qué merece un premio.
levels.challengeEn: Describe a friend you admire: what they are like, what they do, and why they deserve an award.
levels.successEn: Use two or three quality adjectives with correct agreement, -er/-ir verbs (vive, comparte, escribe), and merecer.
levels.sampleAnswerEs: Admiro a mi amigo Daniel. Es honesto y creativo. Vive en Miami y escribe música. Merece un premio.
levels.sampleAnswerEn: I admire my friend Daniel. He is honest and creative. He lives in Miami and writes music. He deserves an award.

levels.challengeEs: Tu primo llega más tarde. Descríbelo para Lupita y di qué prefiere tomar.
levels.challengeEn: Your cousin is arriving later. Describe him for Lupita and say what he prefers to drink.
levels.successEn: Use a possessive (mi primo), two physical adjectives with agreement, and a stem-changing verb (prefiere, quiere).
levels.sampleAnswerEs: Mi primo es alto y moreno, y tiene el pelo corto. Prefiere el agua de jamaica.
levels.sampleAnswerEn: My cousin is tall and dark-skinned, and he has short hair. He prefers the hibiscus water.
